    chore(codex): remove orphaned session-start-codex hook + refresh hook docs
    
    hooks/session-start-codex has had no caller since "Remove Codex hooks"
    (#1845) deleted hooks-codex.json and its manifest registration; the
    Codex manifest now declares an empty hooks object so Codex registers no
    session-start hook at all. The script is Codex-specific dead code —
    nothing executes it on Codex or any other harness.
    
    - Delete hooks/session-start-codex.
    - tests/hooks/test-session-start.sh: drop the two Codex cases that are
      redundant with the generic session-start tests (nested-format and the
      legacy-warning omission are already covered by the Claude Code cases).
      Re-point the "wrapper dispatches" case to the live `session-start`
      script so run-hook.cmd dispatch coverage — used by Claude Code and
      Cursor in production — is preserved rather than lost.
    - docs/porting-to-a-new-harness.md: Codex is no longer a Shape A
      (shell-hook) harness, so re-anchor that worked example to Cursor (a
      live shell-hook harness that demonstrates the same per-harness field,
      schema, and matcher variance) and mark Codex as native skill discovery
      with no session-start hook. Clears the references to the deleted
      hooks-codex.json.
    - docs/windows/polyglot-hooks.md: the "check hooks-codex.json" pointer
      referenced a file deleted in #1845; re-point to hooks-cursor.json.
    
    RELEASE-NOTES.md keeps its historical mention of hooks-codex.json (it
    accurately records what that release did). The tests/codex-plugin-sync
    fixtures build their own synthetic session-start-codex and test the sync
    mechanism generically, so they are intentionally left as-is.

## THREAT MODEL — REQUIRED CONTEXT (read before flagging anything "insecure / bypassable / under-defended")

This plan was DELIBERATELY shrunk from an earlier fortress design. Grade findings against the ACTUAL threat model below, not against a corporate zero-trust ideal. A finding that amounts to "you should re-add adversary defenses" is by-design-rejected unless it names a concrete IRREVERSIBLE footgun that the env-floor does not already close.

**The actual threat model: two trusted mates, not corp-vs-adversary.**
- Pete (non-technical operator) is TRUSTED in intent. He is NOT defended-against. He will trip footguns by accident, not malice.
- The controls exist to catch (a) the coding AGENT's mistakes (it will confidently hardcode a key / delete wrong records), and (b) irreversible effects regardless of good intent. NOT to stop a deliberate insider.
- **DELETED ON PURPOSE (do not recommend re-adding as a "gap"):** immutable CI trust-root, forge-proof hold-ledger, defeat-proof required-checks, blanket-CODEOWNERS, any machinery hardened against a worker/admin trying to BYPASS it. No adversary is trying to defeat these controls.

**THE ENV-FLOOR is the primary control (this is the load-bearing fact).**
- The agent's runtime holds ONLY `gh` + AWS S3 (public website-images bucket). NO prod DB, NO live Stripe/Trello/Mailchimp/MessageBird keys, NO SSH/Forge/deploy.
- Therefore the whole "out-of-git effects" class (agent clicks prod refund button, runs Tinker on prod, deploys) CANNOT happen — there is no credential to reach prod. Do NOT flag out-of-git effects as an unguarded gap; the env-floor closes them. The MCP/browser-target gate is defense-in-depth + UX, not the boundary.
- S3 is public images (no PII/secrets); worst case is a broken image, re-uploaded. Needs no guard.

**The three-tier git model (enforced by stock GitHub at GH-Teams activation, advisory before):**
- REFUSE (secrets) → secret push-protection blocks the PUSH (the enforceable line is the push, not the commit).
- RED (dangerous effects) → pushes + PRs allowed, but CODEOWNERS on red-path globs forces Mark's merge-review.
- GREEN (obvious/reversible) → self-merges when CI green (the `gh` token CAN merge — deliberate, so Pete ships simple changes fast).

**Accepted residuals (eyes-open, NOT findings unless you show they're irreversible):**
- CODEOWNERS is path-based → a RED effect on an unexpected path could self-merge. Reversible; a dial (widen globs).
- Pre-Teams, "RED = not merge" rests on the honor system + env-floor. Known, time-boxed.

**How to review, given the above:**
- "Client prose / advisory check is bypassable" → EXPECTED, by-design. NOT a finding.
- "Re-add [fortress element] to defend against a worker defeating the control" → by-design-rejected. NOT a finding.
- "A concrete IRREVERSIBLE effect (secret leak, prod mutation, data loss) slips past the env-floor AND secret-push-protection" → VALID, high-severity. Flag it with the concrete path.
- Everything else — writing-skills/Iron-Law discipline, task ordering/dependencies, danger-scan CLASSIFICATION correctness (mis-grading under-protects), internal contradictions, vacuous tests, prompt-injection, Pete-facing friction, the SHRINK cutting a control that was actually load-bearing for a NON-adversary reason — grade normally; no free pass.
- Specifically DO probe: **did the shrink go too far?** Did deleting the fortress also delete something that protected against an honest MISTAKE (not an adversary)? That is the highest-value finding for this version.

**DROPPED (the fortress): immutable CI trust-root, forge-proof hold-ledger, defeat-proof required-checks, CODEOWNERS-covers-everything.** No one is trying to defeat the controls.

## `[S]` SERVER — a config checklist, NOT a design problem (flip on at GH-Teams)
Stock GitHub, no custom machinery. Three settings, mapped to the buckets above:

| Setting | Enforces | Bucket |

| **Secret push-protection** | REFUSE class — secret never reaches GitHub (blocks the *push*) | irreversible |
| **CODEOWNERS on red-path globs** → Mark's merge-review | RED class — pushes + PRs, but can't merge without Mark | un-judgeable |

**Tier → git-action (at Teams activation):**

GREEN: with SKILL.md, agent walks intake→danger-scan (button GREEN / key REFUSE / delete RED), holds red items local, routes only green, hits UAT stop, sends Pete one operator-message. Assert: no push of held items, no jargon to Pete, gates hit in order.

### Group B — New judgment grafts (parallel fan-out; each RED-GREEN-REFACTOR)
- **B1 — Intake bundle.** RED: baseline (a) asks Pete a code-answerable Q, (b) proceeds on unbounded cross-cutting change without listing affected files, (c) asks a context-free Q after a topic switch. GREEN: greps code first + only asks judgment calls; unbounded scope → lists files + waits for Pete OK; re-grounds every Q (what/where/need).
- **B2 — Status contract + SPEC-OBJECTION.** RED: implementer returns "done, minor env issue" (vague) / silently codes around a spec that's internally contradictory. GREEN: emits exactly DONE/DONE_WITH_NOTES/BLOCKED{tried,failed,need}/NEEDS_INFO; raises SPEC-OBJECTION → reopens gate instead of guessing.
- **B3 — Claims-are-hearsay + Evidence Receipt.** RED: reviewer/verifier accepts implementer's "tests pass" and reports done without re-running; headline verdict drawn from narration. GREEN: reviewer re-runs `./run-tests.sh` itself + quotes output; emits receipt separating FACTS (diff SHA, exit code) from ASSESSMENT; "couldn't run" → INVALID (blocking), never a pass.
- **B4 — Goal-backward verify + stub/test-integrity detectors.** RED: agent marks done when `wire:click` is unwired / controller returns hardcoded array / a new PHPUnit test has no assertion tied to source (tautology). GREEN: walks Exists→Substantive→Wired→Data-flows with Laravel greps; flags tautological / no-import / assertion-churn tests.
- **B5 — Finding filter + argument-quality + fix-loop cap.** RED: review surfaces hedge findings ("consider…", "might…") to Pete; fix-loop iterates without bound. GREEN: finding needs mechanism+file:line+consequence or is demoted; confidence×impact drop before Pete sees; loop caps (~3) → escalate to Pete with both sides plain.
- **B6 — Checkpoint taxonomy + batch-UAT.** RED: agent tells Pete to run a terminal command / pauses for verification after every file. GREEN: classifies asks as human-verify/decision/human-action, never CLI; harvests inline `<verify>` blocks into ONE end-of-phase plain doc. **Regression guard:** re-run uat-stop v1's stop+pressure scenarios to confirm batching didn't reopen the "push early" hole.
- **B7 — Stage-gate discipline (spec-review 1b + plan-review 2b).** RED: baseline flows intake→plan→execute with only self-review + Pete's rubber-stamp — never independently interrogates the spec for ambiguity, never reviews the plan for defects/scope-drift before coding; under "just build it" pressure it skips straight to execution. GREEN: STOPS at the spec boundary and runs a devil's-advocate grill (rigor-dialed) surfacing open questions to Pete; STOPS at the plan boundary and runs an independent defect/scope-match/constraints review before advancing; codex inline on red-path; pressure does not release either gate. Satisfies locked "review gate at spec/plan/code" (code half already covered by B3/B5/spine). Devil's-advocate grill = this graft's spec-side mechanism (moved OUT of tier-2 — it's now general-path, depth set by rigor dial).

### Group C — Mechanical hooks (parallel, worktree-isolated; real TDD)
- **C1 — secret-scan PreToolUse.** Failing test: fixture Edit adding a live `sk_live_…`/Mailchimp/Trello/MessageBird key → must block; allowlisted placeholder/`.env.example` ref → passes; `.env`/`.pem` path → refuse. **Interface note:** reconcile with existing pre-push secret scan (don't duplicate; this is the Edit-time layer).
- **C2 — write-lockdown PreToolUse.** Failing test: implementer scoped to `resources/views/livewire/x.blade.php` attempting write to `config/magic.php` or `app/Console/` → block; in-scope write → allow.
- **C3 — frozen-criteria check.** Failing test: editing the acceptance-criteria file after session-start SHA → fail; unchanged → pass.
- **C4 — completion Stop/SubagentStop hook.** Failing test: end turn with a declared phase lacking an evidence entry in the state file → blocked; all-evidenced → allowed.
- **C5 — MCP gate (effect ∧ target).** Failing test: `Tinker`/`RecordRule`/`browser_run_code_unsafe`/`browser_evaluate` call → deny; read-only boost tool → allow; playwright pointed at a prod origin → deny, at Herd/test.jointly.shop → allow.
- **C6 — path-fence glob→tier.** Failing test: diff touching a red glob (money/auth/migrations/config/CI) → forces review tier ≥ medium regardless of self-assessed complexity.

### Group D — Config wiring (main loop; after C exists)
- **D1 — CLAUDE.md router:** stage→skill map, rigor dial, path globs, refusal list. Test: light (loads; a routing spot-check subagent picks the right skill for 3 sample requests).
- **D2 — settings.json + SessionStart frame + UserPromptSubmit marker nudge.** Test: hooks register (use `/update-config` skill); SessionStart injects frame.

## PART IV — Ordering & parallelism

```
[ B1 B2 B3 B4 B5 B6 B7 ]  ∥  [ C1 C2 C3 C4 C5 C6 ]   ← two parallel fan-outs (Workflow)
                    │
                    ▼
                   A1  (compose skeleton — main loop, needs B*+C* + DONE grafts)
                    │
                    ▼
                   A2  (end-to-end composition test — the integration gate)
                    │
                    ▼
                   D1, D2  (config wiring)
                    │
                    ▼
        final whole-skill review (multi-review / superpowers:requesting-code-review)
```

- **B** runs as a Haiku/Sonnet writing-skills fan-out (each graft independent — matches the pattern used twice this session).
- **C** runs worktree-isolated (hooks mutate files in parallel).
- **A, D** stay in the main loop — composition needs the whole picture; too much cross-graft context to delegate blind.
- **Rationale for NOT wrapping in SDD:** the shape is parallel-independent-authoring → single-point compose, which is Workflow + main-loop. SDD's sequential-implementer-with-code-review-between fits code tasks, not a batch of independent doc RED-GREEN loops. (Deviation from writing-plans' default SDD handoff, stated with reason.)
